title: ICC Docket 25-0175 — Order - Final: Final Order
text:
STATE OF ILLINOIS 

ILLINOIS COMMERCE COMMISSION 

J & R Appliances, Inc. 

: 

: 
Application for Certification as an Installer : 
25-0175 
of Distributed Generation Facilities under 
: 
Section 16-128A of the Public Utilities Act. : 

ORDER 

By the Commission: 
I. 
INTRODUCTION 

On February 24, 2025, J & R Appliances, Inc. (“Applicant” or “Company”) filed a 
verified Application with the Illinois Commerce Commission (“Commission”) requesting a 
certificate of service authority to operate as an installer of distributed generation facilities 
in Illinois pursuant to Section 16-128A of the Public Utilities Act (“Act”). 220 ILCS 5/16-
128A. The Applicant requests authority to offer services as an Installer of Distributed 
Generation Facilities for photovoltaic types of distributed generation technology in the 
State of Illinois. On June 11, 2026, Staff of the Commission (“Staff”) filed a Certified 
Statement recommending that the Commission grant the requested certificate of service 
authority. The Administrative Law Judge waived the hearing in this matter, entered Staff’s 
Certified Statement into the record and marked the record “Heard & Taken.” 
II. 
REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL APPLICANTS UNDER SECTION 16-128A OF THE 
ACT 

The Applicant has provided all pertinent contact information for itself as well as 
those persons or entities responsible for issues related to processing of the Application 
and Applicant’s applicable federal employer identification number or taxpayer 
identification number. The Applicant agrees to comply with informational and reporting 
requirements established in Section 468.50 of the Commission’s Rules. 83 Ill. Adm. Code 
468.50. In addition, the Applicant agrees to accept service by electronic means as 
provided under the Commission’s Rules of Practice. 83 Ill. Adm. Code 200.1050. The 
Application also includes the following information regarding the person who will perform 
or directly supervise installation to satisfy the requirements of Section 468.50: 
1. A copy of the certification of satisfactory completion of the relevant training 
programs; and/or 
2. An Affidavit by each qualifying person attesting to having satisfactorily completed 
at least five (5) installations of distributed generation facilities for photovoltaic 
distributed generation technology. 

25-0175 
2 
III. 
CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS UNDER SECTION 468.60 

Applicant has demonstrated that it meets the following five (5) requirements in 
Section 468.60: 
a) 
It will remain in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations and 
Commission rules and orders, including, but not limited to, the requirements 
of Sections 16-128(a) and 16-128A of the Act and Section 468. 
b) 
It will ensure that its employees, agents or contractors, or the employees, 
agents or contractors of any entity, agent or contractor with which he has 
contracted to perform those functions within the State of Illinois, shall: 
1) 
Comply with applicable building and electrical codes, including those 
contained in the National Electric Code; 
2) 
Comply with the distributed generation facility manufacturer's 
installation instructions; 
3) 
Install only distributed generation facilities that meet recognized 
industry standards; and 
4) 
Ensure that all obligations required under this Section and Sections 
16-128(a) and 16-128A of the Act are met prior to placing into, or 
returning into, use any distributed generation facility that the 
certificate holder installed. 
c) 
It will comply with applicable licensing and municipal bonding requirements 
to do business in the State of Illinois. 
d) 
Every installation of a distributed generation facility will be performed only 
by: 
1) 
A qualified person; or 
2) 
An electrical contractor who is not a qualified person, provided 
he/she is directly supervised by a qualified person; or 
3) 
a person who is not a qualified person but is enrolled in a training 
program that, upon satisfactory completion, will meet the 
requirement to become a qualified person, provided he/she is 
directly supervised by a qualified person. 
e) 
It is licensed to do business in the State of Illinois. 
IV. 
CONSUMER COMPLAINTS 
The Applicant states that it is not certified or licensed to operate as an Installer of 
Distributed Generation Facilities in any other state. It also declares in it has not received 
any consumer complaints over the last five years. 
V. 
COMMISSION CONCLUSION AND CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE AUTHORITY 

The Commission has reviewed the Application and attachments provided by 
Applicant and finds that the Applicant sufficiently demonstrates compliance with the 
requirements of the Act and Part 468. Staff reviewed the Application and recommended 

25-0175 
3 
that the Applicant be granted a certificate of service authority as an Installer of Distributed 
Generation Facilities. The Commission concludes, therefore, that the Applicant’s request 
for a certificate of service authority to operate as an Installer of Distributed Generation 
Facilities for photovoltaic types of distributed generation technology in Illinois should be 
granted and should include the following authority: 
CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE AUTHORITY 

IT IS CERTIFIED that J & R Appliances, Inc. is granted 
service authority to operate as an Installer of Distributed 
Generation Facilities for photovoltaic types of distributed 
generation technology in the State of Illinois. 
VI. 
FINDINGS AND ORDERING PARAGRAPHS 

The Commission, having reviewed the entire record, is of the opinion and finds 
that: 
(1) 
J & R Appliances, Inc. is authorized to transact business in Illinois and seeks 
a certificate of service authority to operate as an Installer of Distributed 
Generation Facilities for photovoltaic types of distributed generation 
technology under Section 16-128A of the Act; 
(2) 
the Commission has jurisdiction over the party hereto and the subject matter 
hereof; 
(3) 
the recitals of fact and conclusions reached in the prefatory portion of this 
Order are supported by the record and are hereby adopted as findings of 
fact; 
(4) 
J & R Appliances, Inc. has demonstrated that it possesses sufficient 
certification and experience to provide services as an Installer of Distributed 
Generation Facilities for photovoltaic types of distributed generation 
technology in the State of Illinois; 
(5) 
J & R Appliances, Inc. has complied with Section 16-128A of the Act and 
Part 468 and has not been the subject of any consumer complaints in any 
state; and 
(6) 
J & R Appliances, Inc. should be granted a certificate of service authority to 
operate as an Installer of Distributed Generation Facilities for photovoltaic 
types of distributed generation technology as specified in this Order. 

IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED by the Illinois Commerce Commission that J & R 
Appliances, Inc. is hereby granted a Certificate of Service Authority to operate as an 
Installer of Distributed Generation Facilities for photovoltaic types of distributed 
generation technology; said Certificate of Service Authority shall read as that set forth in 
Section V of this Order. 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that J & R Appliances, Inc. shall comply with the 
recertification requirements in 83 Ill. Adm. Code 468.80. 

IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that J & R Appliances, Inc. shall comply with all 
applicable Commission rules and orders now and as hereafter amended. 

25-0175 
4 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that pursuant to Section 10-113(a) of the Public 
Utilities Act and 83 Ill. Adm. Code 200.880, any application for rehearing shall be filed 
within 30 days after service of the Order on the party. 

IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that, subject to the provisions of Section 10-113 of the 
Public Utilities Act and 83 Ill. Adm. Code 200.880, this Order is final; it is not subject to 
the Administrative Review Law. 

By Order of the Commission this 1st day of July, 2026. 

(SIGNED) DOUGLAS P. SCOTT 

Chairman

certificate of service authority. The Administrative Law Judge issued rulings on May 8, 
2026 and May 27, 2026. In response to those rulings, Applicant filed Amended 
Applications on May 26, 2026 and June 11, 2026. Since all of the information to grant 
the requested relief was contained in the Application, the Administrative Law Judge 
waived the hearing in this matter, admitted Staff’s Certified Statement into the record, and 
marked the record “Heard and Taken.” 
II. 
REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL APPLICANTS UNDER SECTION 16-128A OF THE 
ACT 

Applicant has provided all pertinent contact information for itself as well as those 
persons or entities responsible for issues related to processing of the Application and 
Applicant’s applicable federal employer identification number or taxpayer identification 
number as required by Section 469.40 of the Commission’s rules. 83 Ill. Adm. Code 
469.40. Applicant also agrees to comply with informational and reporting requirements 
established in Section 469.50. In addition, Applicant agrees to accept service by 
electronic means as provided under the Commission’s Rules of Practice, 83 Ill. Adm. 
Code 200.1050. The Application includes the following information regarding the person 
who will perform or directly supervise installation to satisfy the requirements of Section 
469.40(f): 
1. 
A copy of the certification of satisfactory completion of the relevant training 
programs; and/or 

26-0169 
2 
2. 
An Affidavit by each qualifying person attesting to having satisfactorily 
completed at least five (5) installations of electric vehicle charging stations. 
III. 
CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS UNDER SECTION 469.50 

Applicant is required by Section 469.50 of the Commission’s rules to certify that it 
meets the following five (5) requirements: 
a) 
It will remain in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations and 
Commission rules and orders, including, but not limited to, the requirements 
of Sections 16-128(a) and 16-128A of the Act and Section 469. 
b) 
It will ensure that its employees, agents or contractors that install, maintain 
or repair electric vehicle charging stations or the employees, agents or 
contractors of any entity, agent or contractor with which it has contracted to 
perform those functions within the State of Illinois, shall: 
1) 
Comply with applicable building and electrical codes, including those 
contained in the National Electric Code; 
2) 
Comply with the electric vehicle charging station manufacturer’s 
installation, maintenance and repair instructions; 
3) 
Install only electric vehicle charging stations that meet the standards 
UL2202 – Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging System Equipment, 
UL2231-1 – Personnel Protection Systems for Electric Vehicle (EV) 
Supply Circuits: General Requirements, UL2231-2 – Personnel 
Protection Systems for Electric Vehicle (EV) Supply Circuits: 
Particular Requirements for Protection Devices for Use in Charging 
System and UL2594 – Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment, 
developed by the Underwriters Laboratory, 333 Pfingsten Road, 
Northbrook IL 60062; 
4) 
Ensure that all installer, maintainer or repairer obligations required 
under this Part and Sections 16-128(a) and 16-128A of the Act are 
met prior to the placing into, or returning into, use any electric vehicle 
charging station that the certificate holder installed, maintained or 
repaired; and 
5) 
Submit notifications to the servicing electric utility in accordance with 
the requirements specified in the applicable tariffs of the servicing 
electric utility, Section 16-128A of the Act, and this Part. 
c) 
It will comply with applicable municipal licensing and bonding requirements 
to do business in the State of Illinois. 
d) 
It will ensure that every installation, maintenance and repair of an electric 
vehicle charging station will be performed only by: 
1) 
A qualified person; or 

26-0169 
3 
2) 
An electrical contractor who is licensed in at least one municipality in 
the State of Illinois who is not a qualified person, provided he/she is 
directly supervised by a qualified person; or 
3) 
A person who is enrolled in a training program that, upon satisfactory 
completion, will meet the requirement to become a qualified person 
provided he/she is directly supervised by a qualified person. 
e) 
It affirms that it is licensed to do business in the State of Illinois. 
IV. 
CERTIFICATIONS/LICENSES AND CONSUMER COMPLAINTS 
Applicant states it is not certified or licensed to install, maintain or repair electric 
vehicle charging station facilities in any other state. Applicant also declares it has not 
received consumer complaints in any state in the last five years. 
V. 
COMMISSION CONCLUSION AND CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE AUTHORITY 

The Commission has reviewed the Application, Amended Applications, and 
attachments provided by Applicant and finds that Applicant sufficiently demonstrates 
compliance with the requirements of the Act and Part 469. Staff recommends that the 
Commission grant the Application. The Commission concludes, therefore, that 
Applicant’s request for a certificate of service authority to operate as an Installer, 
Maintainer or Repairer of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations in Illinois should be granted 
and should include the following authority:

IT IS CERTIFIED that T.A. Electrical Contracting, Inc. 
is granted service authority to operate as an Installer, 
Maintainer or Repairer of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations 
in the State of Illinois. 
VI. 
FINDINGS AND ORDERING PARAGRAPHS 

The Commission, having reviewed the entire record, is of the opinion and finds 
that: 
(1) 
T.A. Electrical Contracting, Inc. is authorized to transact business in Illinois

16-128A of the Act; 
(2) 
the Commission has jurisdiction over the party hereto and the subject matter 
hereof; 
(3) 
the recitals of fact and conclusions reached in the prefatory portion of this

fact; 
(4)

Applicant has complied with Section 16-128A of the Act and Part 469;

INTRODUCTION

Section 16-115C of the Public Utilities Act (“Act”), 220 ILCS 5/1-101 et seq., and 83 Ill. 
Adm. Code 454, "Licensure of Retail Electric Agents, Brokers and Consultants" (“Part 
454”). Applicant requests authority to offer services as an ABC for the procurement or 
sale of retail electricity supply for third parties in the State of Illinois. On June 5, 2026, 
Staff of the Commission (“Staff”) filed a Verified Statement recommending that the 
Commission grant the requested certificate of service authority. The Administrative Law 
Judge (“ALJ”) waived the hearing in this matter, entered Staff’s Verified Statement into 
the record and marked the record “Heard and Taken”. 
II. 
REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL APPLICANTS UNDER SECTION 16-115C OF THE 
ACT

transact business in Illinois. Applicant has certified that it will comply with all applicable 
regulations; that it will comply with informational and reporting requirements established 
by Commission rule; that it will comply with informational and reporting requirements 
pursuant to Section 16-115C of the Act; and that it will comply with all other applicable 
laws, regulations, terms, and conditions required to the extent they have application to 
the services being offered by an ABC. Applicant has agreed to ensure that any person 
who acts on its behalf will comply with all applicable sections of Part 454. Applicant 
agrees that it will remain in compliance with the provisions of the Act and Part 454, and 
will ensure that authorizations received from customers, and all other applicable records

Attachment 1 to the Application contains a corporate organizational chart and identifies

authorized to transact business in Illinois, seeks a certificate of service 
authority to operate as an ABC under Section 16-115C of the Act; 
(2) 
the Commission has jurisdiction over the party hereto and the subject matter 
hereof;

INTRODUCTION 
On December 30, 2025, Under the Sun Solar Limited (“Applicant”) filed a verified 
Application with the Illinois Commerce Commission (“Commission”) requesting a 
certificate of service authority to operate as an installer of energy efficiency measures in 
Illinois pursuant to Section 16 128B of the Public Utilities Act (“Act”). 220 ILCS 5/16-
128B. On February 25, 2026, the Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”) issued a ruling 
directing Applicant to revise the certificate of insurance to list the Illinois Commerce 
Commission as a certificate holder. Applicant did not file any response to the ruling. A 
Proposed Order was issued on April 27, 2026. No briefs on exceptions were filed. 
II. 
THE APPLICATION 
Part 462 of the Commission’s rules sets forth requirements for applicants seeking 
a certificate of authority to install energy efficiency measures in the State of Illinois. 83 
Ill. Adm. Code 462. The information provided in the Application is not sufficient to show 
that the Applicant meets the requirements to be approved as an installer of energy 
efficiency measures in Illinois. Section 462.50 of the Commission’s rules requires 
Applicants to be licensed to do business in Illinois. The Administrative Law Judge issued 
a ruling directing Applicant to update the certificate of insurance on February 25, 2026. 
Applicant did not respond to the ruling and did not respond to the Proposed Order issued 
by the ALJ on April 27, 2026. 
III. 
COMMISSION ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSION 
The Commission reviewed the Application and attachments provided by the 
Applicant and finds that the Applicant did not demonstrate compliance with the 
requirements of the Act and Part 462 of the Commission’s rules. The Commission finds 
that Applicant has failed to meet the requirements necessary to justify recommendation 
for a certificate of authority to install energy efficiency measures in the State of Illinois 
under the Act and Part 462 of the Commission’s rules. The Commission therefore 
concludes that the Applicant’s request for a certificate of authority to install energy 
efficiency measures in Illinois should be denied. 

25-1102 
2 
IV. 
FINDINGS AND ORDERING PARAGRAPHS 

The Commission, having reviewed the entire record, is of the opinion and finds

Under the Sun Solar Limited seeks a certificate of service authority to

128A of the Act;

the Commission has jurisdiction over the party hereto and the subject matter 
hereof;

the recitals of fact and conclusions reached in the prefatory portion of this 
Order are supported by the record and are hereby adopted as findings of 
fact; 
(4) 
Under the Sun Solar Limited has not complied with Section 16-128A of the 
Public Utilities Act and Part 462 of the Commission’s rules; and 
(5) 
Under the Sun Solar Limited should not be granted a certificate of service 
authority to operate as an Installer of Energy Efficiency Measures in the 
State of Illinois as specified in this Order. 
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED by the Illinois Commerce Commission that Under 
the Sun Solar Limited is hereby denied a Certificate of Service Authority authorizing it to 
operate as an Installer of Energy Efficiency Measures in the State of Illinois.

the Administrative Review Law.

Commission rules and orders now and as hereafter amended. 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that pursuant to Section 10-113(a) of the Public 
Utilities Act and 83 Ill. Adm. Code 200.880, any application for rehearing shall be filed

Public Utilities Act and 83 Ill. Adm. Code 200.880, this Order is final; it is not subject to 
the Administrative Review Law.
